statement:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. By using vectors, or otherwise, prove that:

(i) $AB^2+BC^2+CD^2+DA^2=AC^2+BD^2$;

(ii) $|AC^2-BD^2|$ is $4$ times the area of the rectangle whose sides are *any* side of the parallelogram and the projection of an adjacent side on that side.

State and prove a result like (ii) about $|AB^2-AD^2|$ and the diagonals.
solution:
Let $\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf a$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}=\mathbf b$. Then $\overrightarrow{AC}=\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}=\mathbf a-\mathbf b$.

(i) The four sides have squared lengths $|\mathbf a|^2+|\mathbf b|^2+|\mathbf a|^2+|\mathbf b|^2=2|\mathbf a|^2+2|\mathbf b|^2$. The diagonals give
$$AC^2+BD^2=|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2+|\mathbf a-\mathbf b|^2=(|\mathbf a|^2+2\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+|\mathbf b|^2)+(|\mathbf a|^2-2\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+|\mathbf b|^2)=2|\mathbf a|^2+2|\mathbf b|^2.$$
So the two sums are equal.

(ii) Now
$$AC^2-BD^2=|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2-|\mathbf a-\mathbf b|^2=4\,\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b.$$
Now $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=|\mathbf a|\times(\text{projection of }\mathbf b\text{ onto }\mathbf a)$, so
$$|AC^2-BD^2|=4|\mathbf a|\times|\text{projection of }\mathbf b\text{ on }\mathbf a|,$$
which is $4$ times the area of the rectangle with sides $AB$ and the projection of $AD$ onto $AB$.

**Analogous result for sides and diagonals.** Using $|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2-|\mathbf a-\mathbf b|^2=4\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$ again, we also have, from the diagonals $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf a-\mathbf b$:
$$|AB^2-AD^2|=\bigl||\mathbf a|^2-|\mathbf b|^2\bigr|.$$
Writing the diagonals as $\mathbf u=\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf v=\mathbf a-\mathbf b$, one obtains
$$AB^2-AD^2=\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf a-\mathbf b)+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v,$$
i.e. $|AB^2-AD^2|$ equals the product of the two diagonal lengths times $\cos$ of the angle between them.

[难度自评: Q1是 Q2是 Q3否 Q4是 Q5否 → 4星]
hints: Let AB=a, AD=b, so AC=a+b and BD=a-b.
Note a·b relates to the projection of one side onto the other.
